title: Supreme Court: SAS Institute Inc. v. Iancu
summary: When the United States Patent and Trademark Office institutes an inter partes review to reconsider an already-issued patent claim, see 35 U. S. C. §§311–319, it must decide the patentability of all of the claims the petitioner has challenged. (No. 16-969, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 584 U.S. 357).

title: Supreme Court: Oil States Energy Services, LLC v. Greene’s Energy Group, LLC
summary: Inter partes review—which authorizes the United States Patent and Trademark Office to reconsider and cancel an already-issued patent claim, see 35 U. S. C. §§311–319—does not violate Article III or the Seventh Amendment of the Constitution. (No. 16-712, opinion by Justice Thomas; 584 U.S. 325).

title: Supreme Court: Jesner v. Arab Bank, PLC
summary: The Second Circuit’s judgment—that foreign corporations may not be defendants in suits brought under the Alien Tort Statute—is affirmed. (No. 16-499, opinion by Justice Kennedy; 584 U.S. 241).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Microsoft Corp.
summary: The Second Circuit’s judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded with instructions to dismiss the case as moot. (No. 17-2, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 584 U.S. 236).

title: Supreme Court: Sessions v. Dimaya
summary: The Ninth Circuit’s judgment—that 18 U. S. C. §16(b), which defines violent felony for purposes of the Immigration and Nationality Act’s removal provisions, is unconstitutionally vague—is affirmed. (No. 15-1498, opinion by Justice Kagan; 584 U.S. 148).

title: Supreme Court: Wilson v. Sellers
summary: A federal habeas court reviewing an unexplained state-court decision on the merits should “look through” that decision to the last related state-court decision that provides a relevant rationale and presume that the unexplained decision adopted the same reasoning; the State may rebut the presumption by showing that the unexplained decision most likely relied on different grounds than the reasoned decision below. (No. 16-6855, opinion by Justice Breyer; 584 U.S. 122).

title: Supreme Court: Kisela v. Hughes
summary: Petitioner police officer is entitled to qualified immunity here, where his actions did not violate clearly established statutory or constitutional rights of which a reasonable person would have known. (No. 17-467, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 584 U.S. 100).

title: Supreme Court: Encino Motorcars, LLC v. Navarro
summary: Because service advisors at car dealerships are “salesm[e]n . . . primarily engaged in . . . servicing automobiles,” 29 U. S. C. §213(b)(10)(A), they are exempt from the Fair Labor Standards Act’s overtime-pay requirement. (No. 16-1362, opinion by Justice Thomas; 584 U.S. 79).
